work_order.understanding: The release-notes gate packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs checks category presence, category membership, authors presence, authors-is-an-array, and a one-line body. It never inspects an author value, so `authors: [claude]` passes the gate that exists to keep the published changelog honest and ships to readers as `— thanks @claude`. Re-verified the defect and the whole fix against the real repository this time, not a clone: on a scratch branch taken from the current HEAD, carrying the prototype change plus a temporary note whose only author is `claude`, the real script printed `::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: claude.` and exited 1; with the gate reverted to origin/main and the identical note in place, the same command printed `Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉` and exited 0. The issue's proposed handle-shape check cannot catch this: `claude` is a syntactically perfect GitHub handle, and all 39 distinct author values in the directory pass such a rule. The owner's recorded decision is binding and this plan implements it exactly: credit Shivam-Fl on both shipped notes, and reject agents/bots by a small denylist — `claude`, `github-actions`, and anything ending in `[bot]` case-insensitively — with a test per rule plus a test that Shivam-Fl passes, and no network lookup. The previous plan was rejected on one mechanical defect only, in the verification recipes: it branched the scratch branch from `origin/main`, which at QA time is unpatched, so AC-6 was unsatisfiable. That is fixed below and re-run against the real repository.
work_order.root_cause: validateFile asserts only that `authors` is present and an array; the value of each element is never examined, so any string — a bot login, a first name, a product name — passes the gate that exists to keep the published changelog honest.
work_order.approach: Two halves, one slice. (1) Put the identity rule in a pure, exported, unit-testable helper called from validateFile. It lives in packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs — the existing shared home for release-notes helpers that the check script already imports from — so no new module for one function. The rule is a denylist exactly as decided: lowercase+trim each author, reject if it equals `claude` or `github-actions` or ends in `[bot]` (which already covers `claude[bot]` and `github-actions[bot]`, the logins git history actually shows). The new branch goes after the `Array.isArray(data.authors)` check and before the one-line body check, preserving the existing ordering. (2) Correct the two shipped notes to `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` by editing in place — they are on main. The helper returns the offending values rather than a boolean so the error names what was wrong and what to put instead. No network call: the decision rules it out, and account existence could not distinguish `claude` (not an account) from `Shivam-Fl` (a real account that asked for the change rather than writing it) anyway. Applied the whole change on a scratch branch in this repository, ran the real gate against it five times, then deleted the branch and every probe artifact; `main` is back at 4ebaf1e with a clean tree.

validated_work_order.understanding: The previous plan's DIAGNOSIS was right and I am not rewriting it. The defect it named - the gate never examines an author value, so `authors: [claude]` ships to readers as `— thanks @claude` - was real, the fix works, and QA confirms it: all eight acceptance criteria pass, and T-3 through T-20 show `claude`, `github-actions` and any `[bot]` suffix rejected, people accepted, both shipped notes crediting Shivam-Fl, and the downstream changelog render thanking a real person. What the previous plan got WRONG is that it specified a rule over strings without ever specifying the TYPE CONTRACT of the value the rule is applied to, and specified no behaviour at all for two boundary inputs. The plan asked for a denylist comparison and said 'lowercase+trim each author'; the implementer wrote `author.toLowerCase()` on every element of a YAML flow sequence. `Array.isArray` guarantees the container, not the elements, and js-yaml types `[12345]` as an int, `[null]` as null, `[true]` as a bool and `[["claude"]]` as a nested list - all four shapes a person could plausibly write, all four throwing inside the filter, and nothing between the filter and the top of the script catches it, so the throw escapes `validateFile` as an unhandled rejection. That is BUG-1, and it is a REGRESSION this PR introduces: on base commit 4ebaf1e those same notes exit 0 with 'Validated', so the PR turns a passing gate into a crashing one. The same under-specification produced BUG-2 one level up: the plan listed an empty-list test case without saying what the correct behaviour was, so the implementer supplied a comment asserting that the neighbouring `!data.authors` and `Array.isArray` checks enforce a non-empty list. Neither does - `[]` is truthy, so the first is false, and `Array.isArray([])` is true. The test then documents a guarantee the code does not make, and the published changelog renders '— thanks ' with nobody credited. Both bugs have the same shape, and it is the shape of the plan rather than the implementer: the happy path's rule was specified to the character and the boundary was left to the reader. A gate reads hostile input, so the boundary is the part that matters. This revision specifies the input domain, the behaviour at each boundary, and the message shape at each one. It also closes two pre-existing holes sitting directly on this issue's defect class, which the previous attempt left standing: BUG-3, the gate selecting notes with `--diff-filter=A`, which means editing an existing note to credit a bot passes untouched - so this PR's own two corrections, which are edits, are invisible to the very gate it strengthens - and BUG-4, `reportError` interpolating front matter into a workflow-command line with no escaping, where this PR adds a second sink (the author value) to a channel `category` already used. Both are reproduced below and both are cheap. BUG-5, an unquoted `[bot]` dying in js-yaml before the gate's own message is reached, is pre-existing, is a front-matter robustness question with its own design, and is left out of scope and flagged instead.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The plan specified the identity rule but never the type contract of the values the rule is applied to. `findNonPersonAuthors` calls `author.toLowerCase()` on every element of a YAML flow sequence, and the caller's `Array.isArray(data.authors)` guard establishes the container, not the elements: js-yaml types `authors: [12345]` as int, `[null]` as null, `[true]` as bool and `[["claude"]]` as a nested list, each of which throws inside the filter, and with no try/catch between the filter and the top of the script the throw escapes `validateFile` as an unhandled rejection - converting a gate that exited 0 on those notes into one that exits 1 on a stack trace with no `::error::` and no file name. The identical under-specification one level up produced BUG-2: the plan asked for an empty-list test case without stating the intended behaviour, so the test was given a comment attributing a non-empty-list guarantee to the `!data.authors` and `Array.isArray` checks, and neither enforces it - `[]` is truthy and `Array.isArray([])` is true, so a note can ship crediting nobody and render as '— thanks '.
validated_work_order.approach: Four changes, all inside packages/ci-actions, none touching a forbidden path. (1) BUG-1, in `findNonPersonAuthors`: make the helper TOTAL over its input. Type-check each element first and treat any non-string - number, null, boolean, nested list, object - as an offender, because none of them is a GitHub username; only then normalise and apply the existing denylist and `[bot]`-suffix rules unchanged. The helper's contract becomes 'return every author that is not a credit to a person', which is one coherent job, keeps the existing seven cases green unchanged (they all pass strings), and makes the call site incapable of throwing no matter what YAML produced. Render non-string offenders with JSON.stringify at the call site so the message names them unambiguously: `[12345].join(', ')` happens to yield "12345", but `[null].join(', ')` yields the EMPTY string, which would produce '...not bots or agents: .' and name nothing. (2) BUG-2: tighten the check rather than the comment. Add an explicit `data.authors.length === 0` branch in `validateFile`, with its own message naming the file, so `authors: []` is rejected instead of published as '— thanks '; then correct the empty-list test comment to state what is true after the change. Tightening is the right side of the line here: the hole is reader-visible, and the neighbouring guard plainly intends to close it and fails only because `[]` is truthy; leaving a test that documents a guarantee the code does not make is the worse of the two options QA offered. (3) BUG-3, in the file-selection query: replace the single `--name-only --diff-filter=A` diff with one `--name-status --diff-filter=AM` diff, derive `added` from the rows whose status starts with A so the existing 'No release note added' guard stays byte-identical, and validate the modified rows as well as the added ones. This is strictly additive - no currently-passing branch starts failing for a reason unrelated to its own notes, and the requirement to ADD a note is unchanged. It also closes the loop on this PR's own deliverable: the two notes it corrects are modifications, so until this change the gate could not see them. (4) BUG-4: sanitise at the sink, not at each caller. Add an exported `sanitizeWorkflowCommandData(value)` to util.mjs implementing GitHub's documented escape set for command data - `%`->`%25`, CR->`%0D`, LF->`%0A`, in that order so a value already containing the literal text `%0A` cannot be resurrected into a real newline - and call it on the message inside `reportError`, which covers the author sink this PR added and the category sink that was already there. `:` and `,` are deliberately NOT escaped: they are only special inside the property syntax, and `reportError` emits `::error::${message}` with no properties. Because the check script is a top-level script with side effects and cannot be imported by a test, both new pieces of logic go in util.mjs, the module the script already imports, where they are unit-testable. No network call is introduced anywhere.
